review_candidates.title: Mainframe Developer
review_candidates.description: On Call Support: This role may require participation in an on-call support rotation. Position Description In this role, you will serve as the primary onsite DBA point of contact for database administration, production support, performance optimization, security, and disaster recovery activities. You will collaborate with application developers, architects, QA teams, DevOps, integration teams, offshore delivery teams, and third party partners to design, maintain, and support reliable DB2 environments for enterprise clients. This is an excellent opportunity to work on challenging client engagements, contribute to modernization and cloud related initiatives, and grow your career within a collaborative consulting environment that values technical excellence, initiative, and continuous learning. Your future duties and responsibilities: As a Mainframe DB2 DBA, you will help ensure the performance, stability, security, and availability of enterprise database environments. Your responsibilities will include: Database Design and Architecture Serve as the primary onsite point of contact for DB2 database administration and related activities. Collaborate with application developers and architects to translate logical data models into efficient physical DB2 database designs. Execute DDL for the creation and modification of tables, views, storage groups, and other database objects. Safely manage schema evolution through complex DB2 ALTER activities. Implement and maintain Universal Table Spaces, including PBG and PBR structures, to support effective storage and partitioning strategies. Design, create, and manage DB2 indexes to support data integrity and optimize application access paths. Performance Tuning and Monitoring Write, review, and tune complex SQL queries to improve application performance and minimize CPU consumption. Monitor and troubleshoot DB2 performance issues, including access path concerns, locking, buffer pools, and SQL execution. Analyze EXPLAIN output and other diagnostic information to identify performance bottlenecks and recommend corrective actions. Use Real Time Statistics (RTS) to monitor database health and schedule maintenance activities proactively. Support performance optimization and continuous improvement initiatives across production environments. Database Operations and Automation Execute and monitor DB2 utilities, including LOAD, UNLOAD, REORG, RUNSTATS, COPY, and RECOVER. Manage DB2 space allocation, including PRIQTY and SECQTY, and monitor VSAM datasets to help prevent storage shortages. Develop and maintain JCL and REXX scripts to automate batch processing and routine DBA activities. Use DB2 command level functions to manage database threads, statuses, and operational activities. Leverage DB2 administration and monitoring tools, such as DB2 Admin Tool and Query Monitor, to support efficient database management. Provide production support, investigate incidents, perform root cause analysis, and coordinate timely issue resolution. Security and Business Continuity Administer DB2 security, including GRANT and REVOKE privileges, in alignment with enterprise access policies. Support database security, audit, compliance, and data protection requirements. Develop, test, and execute disaster recovery strategies to support business continuity. Manage image copies, DB2 logs, backup processes, and recovery activities to help ensure timely restoration following an outage. Participate in production readiness reviews, recovery exercises, and operational support activities. Required qualifications to be successful in this role Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical discipline. Equivalent technical experience may be considered. At least 6 years of experience in mainframe database administration, maintenance, and production support. Strong hands-on experience administering IBM DB2 for z/OS, including database design, performance monitoring and tuning, backup and recovery, security, and production support. Working knowledge of mainframe technologies, including COBOL, JCL, CICS, and VSAM, and an understanding of how applications interact with DB2 databases. Experience with DB2 utilities and administration activities, including RUNSTATS, REORG, COPY, RECOVER, LOAD, and UNLOAD. Experience analyzing and resolving DB2 performance issues, including SQL performance and access path concerns. Experience supporting multiple applications within a large enterprise or production environment. Experience coordinating with offshore teams and providing technical direction or guidance. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills. Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills. Demonstrated initiative, sound judgment, and the ability to make informed technical decisions. Ability to evaluate and recommend solutions for moderate to complex database and production support issues. Ability to work onsite in Salt Lake City and collaborate directly with client and delivery teams. Availability to participate in on call support activities.

Position Summary Provides enterprise leadership for the compute, virtualization, storage, and backup platforms that host clinical, business, integration, and infrastructure workloads. The manager is accountable for platform availability, capacity, lifecycle, security, recoverability, automation, and technical standards across on-premises and approved hosted or cloud environments. Compute and Virtualization Platforms Owns engineering and operations for physical servers, virtualization, hyperconverged infrastructure, operating system platforms, clustering, high availability, and supporting management tools. Oversees performance analysis, demand forecasting, licensing, hardware maintenance, and removal of unsupported infrastructure. Enterprise Storage and Data Protection Owns block, file, and object storage services, including performance, capacity, replication, snapshots, ransomware-resilient capabilities, tiering, and lifecycle management. Owns enterprise backup platforms and operational backup services, including policy administration, job monitoring, exception management, immutable protection, off-site or isolated copies, and restoration support. Partners with application, database, cybersecurity, data center, and disaster recovery teams to translate business requirements into recoverability, retention, replication, and restoration designs. Regularly validates backup success, restoration procedures, recovery dependencies, and evidence required for audits and risk management. Maintains clear accountability between backup operations, disaster recovery orchestration, application recovery, and business continuity. Service Management and Leadership Leads incident, problem, change, release, and capacity management for platform services and serves as executive escalation for significant availability or data protection events. Manages engineering standards, technical documentation, inventories, ownership records, support runbooks, maintenance windows, and operational metrics. Builds a multi-year investment roadmap and manages capital and operating budgets, contracts, licensing, support agreements, vendor performance, and professional services. Leads workforce planning, hiring, coaching, cross-training, succession planning, and a sustainable on-call model. Coordinates infrastructure readiness for application implementations, acquisitions, migrations, data center changes, and cloud or hosted service adoption. Other Responsibilities Participates in an on-call leadership rotation and responds to significant service disruptions outside normal business hours. Minimum Education Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. Minimum Experience Seven or more years of progressive experience in enterprise compute, virtualization, storage, or backup, including at least three years leading technical staff or a major platform service. Other Azure integrations Provide L2/L3 support for other event-driven and API-based Azure integrations (Logic Apps, Function Apps): monitoring, incident resolution, connector and credential maintenance, and minor enhancements through Azure DevOps and change control. Maintain certificates, secrets and connector authorisations for these integrations, and renew them before expiry. Problem management and knowledge Raise problem records for recurring failure patterns such as silent stalls and data-error categories, and track permanent fixes with L3. Maintain the runbook, KQL query library, handoff log, alert catalogue and knowledge articles. Retire superseded wiki content. Create and maintain Azure DevOps work items for defects and improvements handed to L3. Participate in knowledge transfer from the incumbent provider, demonstrate independent handling of common support scenarios, and transfer knowledge to new team members. Security and compliance Use privileged and production access only through the approved access process (e.g. CyberArk), on a least-privilege basis and for authorised tasks. Never record passwords, tokens or other secrets in tickets, email or documents. Store and hand over credentials only through the approved vault. Handle customer, employee and payroll personal information in line with the Privacy Act and Cleanaway data classification, including compliant incident records and escalation of potential data breaches. Maintain segregation of duties: perform data corrections, approvals and production changes only with documented business or change approval, and keep an audit trail. Role boundaries L2/L3 accountability Own shift health checks, monitoring, incident triage, documented recovery, alert build-out and escalation packages for the customer integration platform. Own L2/L3 support for other event-driven and API-based Azure integrations in scope. Function Apps and Logic Apps that run as steps within batch data pipelines belong to the ADF/Databricks engineer. Retain ServiceNow ownership and stakeholder communication while L3 performs code-level remediation. Outside delegated authority Code changes to the customer integration platform's App Services and Function Apps, which belong to the L3 application teams unless formally transferred. Platform architecture, Service Bus topology and APIM policy design. Business decisions on customer master data, matching and survivorship rules owned by MDM and business data owners. Skills and experience Essential Demonstrated production support of Azure integration services: Service Bus (topics, subscriptions, dead-letter queues), App Services and Function Apps, API Management. Application Insights, Log Analytics and KQL for diagnosis, plus Azure Monitor alerting and dashboards. Ability to read structured .NET application logs and trace distributed transactions. ITIL-aligned incident, problem and change practice using ServiceNow or equivalent. Shift handoff discipline. Clear, compliance-aware incident communication with business and technical stakeholders. Desirable Salesforce, MDM (e.g. Ataccama), JD Edwards or AMCS integration experience. Azure Logic Apps, Key Vault, Azure DevOps and ARM/Bicep deployments. Experience raising and managing Microsoft Azure support cases. AZ-900, AZ-104, AZ-204, ITIL 4 Foundation, SC-900. Key relationships L3 application teams (customer integration platform): Code-level defects, running-but-idle interventions, releases and responsibility matrix MDM team, Salesforce support and ERP application teams: Source-data correction and cross-system recovery Cleanaway Integration L2 lead: Priorities, escalation, on-call model and readiness sign-off Service Desk / L1: Intake, initial triage, shift-left knowledge articles and incident escalation Technical Platform Owner / Principal Analyst: Platform priorities, risks, technical governance and acceptance Change and release management: CAB approval, controlled releases and production validation Infrastructure, DBA and Cyber Security teams: Servers, databases, privileged access, certificates and security approvals Performance measures Incident response and resolution against agreed service levels and business-critical processing windows. Completion and effectiveness of proactive monitoring, exception detection and recovery. Service request timeliness and first-time-right fulfilment. Changes delivered successfully through change control, without unplanned outage or rollback. Reduction in repeat incidents through problem records, root cause analysis and permanent fixes. Accuracy and currency of runbooks, knowledge articles, ServiceNow resolution notes and operational documentation. Stakeholder satisfaction and timely communication during incidents and changes. Every shift health check completed and handoff recorded. No undetected backlogs or stalls. Alert rules and baselines implemented and maintained for the platform. Transition readiness (by 21 December 2026) Independence criteria Fujitsu must demonstrate before taking over from the incumbent provider. Remove this section after transition acceptance. Each step requires demonstrated cross-system triage, Microsoft Azure support escalation, disaster-recovery procedures and compliance-aware incident communication. L2/L3 responsibility matrix agreed with the L3 application teams. Alert rules and baselines in place. Incident SLAs met for four consecutive weeks.
